about: One record per detector and per repository-level check: the corpus it was measured on, the date, the counts before and after each calibration, the named exclusions, and where the prose account lives. 'Measured before built' applied to the tool itself. A record whose corpus is null says so: a threshold set by convention is not a measurement, and a claim that cannot be traced is not a claim. Tests/test_calibration.py holds every registered detector to having a record.

records.name: dead_code
exclusions: Protocol and ABC interface classes
string-keyed dynamic dispatch (registry['Name'], exec() into a dict)
disclosed: getattr-by-string and decorator-based registration are not traced; the tool's own @register self-flags

records.name: long_function
disclosed: threshold of 80 lines set by convention, never calibrated on a corpus; a line-count proxy, not cyclomatic complexity
records.source: README, ghost_buster; the finding's own detail text

records.name: near_duplicate_function
exclusions: byte-identical file groups fingerprinted once (duplicate_file's finding)
min_lines 10, not 6
test-only clusters INFORMATIONAL

records.name: intra_function_duplicate_block
exclusions: a single statement counts only across distinct statement lists
single-statement complexity floor 20 nodes (gate.py's four branch returns measured 41, 26, 33, 22)
disclosed: 643 of 655 first-run findings were pairs of similar statements inside one block: how code is written, not a ghost

records.name: doc_test_count_drift
records.corpus: HERALD (135 claimed, 321 collected); ghost_tools self-scan (3 of 3 drift findings false before 0.10.1)
exclusions: one-directional: only a documented count the real count has grown well past (min_growth_ratio and min_absolute_growth both required)
disclosed: the static test_* count is a lower bound; parametrize only pushes the true count higher

records.name: merge_conflict_marker
records.corpus: its own module and tests, which discuss the marker strings in prose
exclusions: the full <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> triplet in order, never a lone line (a Setext H1 underline is a run of =)

records.name: duplicate_file
exclusions: empty files are never a group

records.name: drifted_copy
exclusions: byte-identical groups (duplicate_file's finding)
at least three shared top-level names, equality not overlap
disclosed: does not guess intent: a _v1.1 beside a _v1.2 may be a deliberate archive

records.name: swallowed_exception
exclusions: test files
contextlib.suppress
disclosed: only pass; continue, return None and a lone logger.debug each need their own measurement first

records.name: dead_end_call
exclusions: Null*/NoOp*/Fake*/Stub*/Dummy*/Mock* on a word boundary
definitions and call sites in test files
empty __init__, __enter__, __exit__, __del__
disclosed: cannot say never: an implementation in a repository the scan was not pointed at would settle it
AST-only, no type resolution

records.name: unassessable_file
records.corpus: three files: one clean, one with conflict markers, one with a syntax typo
disclosed: borrowed from observe-perceive's BayesianFusion abstained=True
records.source: README, files that will not parse; CHANGELOG 0.13.0

records.name: name_disagreement
exclusions: only a bijection
a CONSTANT on either side
a leading underscore on one side only
camelCase in a snake_case library
a method only through self or cls; a library-wide name only if defined exactly once
disclosed: reports, never renames

records.name: vestigial_domain_name
disclosed: a prose-shaped identifier check was prototyped on the same corpus: 1,108 hits, 1,099 of them deliberate test names; abandoned

records.name: placeholder_name
exclusions: test files
disclosed: only where decidable from the code; never whether a name is good

records.name: sql_injection
exclusions: the string has to open with a SQL statement keyword (a task runner's execute(f'step {n}') stays silent)
records.source: README, what AI-written code gets wrong; CHANGELOG 0.17.0

records.name: destructive_sql
exclusions: only an executed literal

records.name: insecure_default
exclusions: test files
wide-open CORS without credentials
disclosed: each rule is a construct with essentially one meaning

records.name: unauthenticated_route
exclusions: a fully public module
a fully protected module
auth applied by middleware (drops below the majority threshold)
test files
disclosed: fails quiet, deliberately

records.name: loop_invariant_call
exclusions: another call receives the same name
a method is called on the argument
a store into the argument
a memo behind a None check
a fresh accumulator the loop fills
disclosed: a static pitstop is a hypothesis; only the profiler is evidence

records.name: list_membership_in_loop
exclusions: a literal of eight elements or fewer
disclosed: the tree cannot tell a list of four from a list of four million

records.name: test_status
records.corpus: four real suites: gsa-815 (17 uncollectable modules), observe-perceive (47 skips naming an absent checkout), sentinel_os (18 setup errors on a missing system executable), and a fixture
exclusions: failure text classified from its error lines only, never the walked source
disclosed: a bare assertion whose real cause is a missing service reads as failing
a named service is not probed
a skip condition is not parsed, only its reason

records.name: committed_secret
exclusions: shape-only rules (generic-api-key, curl-auth-header) rate MAJOR, provider-prefix rules CRITICAL
disclosed: a fix scoped to the rules a measurement saw fire is scoped to the measurement

records.name: unmerged_branch
records.corpus: ghost_tools' own history (four squash-merged branches), then 37 repositories
exclusions: whole-branch patch-id comparison against a squash commit
disclosed: cannot see pull-request state
a remote ref deleted on GitHub reads as unmerged until pruned

records.name: structure
records.corpus: ghost_tools (68 modules) and one real repository declaring every import
exclusions: boundaries call-based where the import is noisy
an import that cannot be mapped to a distribution goes to unresolved
disclosed: never infers an architectural boundary from a directory name

records.name: boundary
records.corpus: observe-perceive joined to the six repositories that feed it; ghost_tools self-scan
exclusions: a guarded stdlib import
re-exports and src layouts resolved
disclosed: duck-typed contracts go to unresolved, named

records.name: no_ci_configuration
exclusions: a repository with neither tests nor a deploy artifact

records.name: kernel
records.corpus: a 24-class kernel against 37 repositories, three passes
exclusions: overlap gate 0.5 on methods when the kernel class has any, class-level members otherwise
the kernel's own files inside the tree
test files
disclosed: a member-less class with a different base has nothing to compare

records.name: corpus
disclosed: six read policies collapsed to the interpreter's own

records.name: ledger
disclosed: thresholds (three returns, ten runs, five blind runs) set by design, not measured on a corpus; the trajectory filter is the constant-velocity Kalman filter from a pediatric deterioration engine

records.name: readiness
records.corpus: three operations on ghost_tools, then 38 repositories in the pre-flight sweep
disclosed: unknown counts against the patient

since 1.2.2 only an established credential (CRITICAL) fails the secrets criterion; a candidate is reported beside the verdict and retired by a false decision in the case file. Before that any committed_secret failed it: seven of 38 repositories in the pre-flight sweep, none a credential on the evidence
